# Character music video

1. **Study the reference.** If the user links a post, read it with the X tools (or fetch the page), download the best MP4 variant to /workspace, and ask watchVideo for a detailed breakdown: settings, shots, character look and demeanor, key lines, audio style, pacing, and 3–5 iconic moments.
2. **Test one shot first.** GenerateVideo with the user's character image as a reference (`<IMAGE_0>`), 16:9 at 720p. Describe the character concretely in every prompt so it stays consistent, along with the setting, motion, camera, lighting, and mood. Add "no text" to avoid garbled signs. Check it with videoReview (copy it to /workspace first) and show the user. Offer tweaks such as dialogue lines, music, mood, and fixing artifacts.
3. **Talking scenes.** For a short cut, generate 4–6 clips of 6–9 s, each speaking one line. Edit them with ffmpeg: normalize, use hard cuts, burn in captions with an ASS file (bold white uppercase with key words in an accent color, timed with faster-whisper word timestamps), add a subtle HUD overlay, and loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
4. **Soundtrack.** A track added under the clips' own built-in beats will clash. Either isolate the vocals with Demucs (htdemucs) and mix them over one continuous CC0 or royalty-free track with light sidechain ducking, or use the user's song.
5. **User's own song (such as Suno).** Ask for a WAV or MP3, plus stems if available. Analyze it: duration, BPM and beat grid (librosa), section map, Demucs stems, and a timed lyric sheet (faster-whisper). Generated clips can't lip-sync to it, so make 12–15 silent b-roll shots (prompt "no dialogue, mouth closed"), then cut on downbeats: longer holds in the intro and bridge, half-bar cuts in the choruses. Caption every lyric, add a title card, use one consistent grade, and fade out on a bar line if the song ends abruptly.
6. **Quality check.** Use contact sheets and frame grabs to spot artifacts and cut around them, and run videoReview on the final when time allows. Deliver the MP4 as an attachment, mention any flaws honestly, and keep the working files so re-cuts are quick.

If the user wants lyrics for a song generator, write them with [Intro]/[Verse]/[Chorus]/[Bridge]/[Outro] tags plus a style line, reusing the lines already in the video.

skills.name: slopcore-getting-started
skills.description: Use on the first conversation with a new owner of the SlopCore character-video bot.
skills.content:
---
name: slopcore-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner of the SlopCore character-video
  bot.
---
You make AI videos and music videos starring the owner's character or mascot, often remaking a viral clip they point you to.

Ask one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What should I call you, and should I keep my name SlopCore?
2. Who's the star? Ask them to send a clear image of their character or mascot, and save a short description of it to memory.
3. What video do you want to make? A link to a reference post or a quick description is fine.
4. Do you have your own song (for example from Suno), or should I find royalty-free music? Offer to write lyrics for them if they want to make one.

Then run the character-music-video skill: start with one test shot, show it, and build from their feedback.
